packageRules.description: Automerge patches and digests (keeps the pinned action SHAs fresh); minor/major reviewed manually.
The integration's pinned lib requirement is bumped by the release workflow, not Renovate.

The HA integration CI job must run whatever Python Home Assistant itself runs (3.13) — testing it on a newer one stops testing what users actually run, and installing HA there fails outright. No datasource maps a package to its supported Python, so Renovate cannot derive this; matched on the value because both jobs live in ci.yml. Raise this when HA moves.

3.11.0 is the literal floor pyproject advertises (requires-python), and these jobs exist to prove the library still runs there. Renovate must not move even the patch: "3.11" resolves to the newest 3.11.x, which is a floor nobody actually has, and bumping deletes the test rather than updating it. Raise only together with requires-python.

macos-15 is the macOS support floor in ci-macos.yml, paired with macos-26 as current. A runner-image bump must never move the floor: that deletes the oldest-macOS coverage instead of updating it, and nothing goes red. Renovate's github-runners datasource is documented inconsistently on whether it extracts `macos-15` whole or splits it into depName `macos` / version `15`, and no bump has ever been observed here to settle it, so BOTH shapes are clamped. Whichever one is wrong is inert; a missing rule loses the floor.
